title: Geometric gluing of local universal thickening charts
statement: Let h : Z → X be a morphism of schemes, C an open cover of Z indexed in the schemes universe, and for every k let i_k : C_k → Z′_k and h′_k : Z′_k → X be a universal first order thickening of C_k over X for C.f_k ≫ h [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]. There exist W, j : Z → W, p : W → X and an open cover D of W in the same universe such that j is a first order thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], j ≫ p = h, and for every k the pullback of j along D.f_k is universal over X for the induced source morphism. No formal unramifiedness hypothesis and no global universal lifting property is asserted.

source.place: Tag 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), proof, fourth and fifth paragraphs; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04F3

proof.text: For each pair of open charts of C, restrict the two supplied universal thickenings to their intersection. The unique corresponding open exists because a first order thickening is a homeomorphism. The restricted thickenings remain universal over X by the open-pieces theorem, taking the whole base open.

The uniqueness theorem for universal thickenings identifies the two restricted thickenings by the unique isomorphism over X fixing the intersection. On a triple intersection the direct transition and the composite transition are morphisms between the same universal thickenings extending the same identity, so uniqueness makes them equal. Repeated indices give the identity. These are exactly the overlap and cocycle identities for scheme gluing.

Apply scheme gluing to the local schemes and their open transition isomorphisms. Its canonical open immersions cover a scheme W. The local maps to X agree on overlaps, hence glue to p. The maps from the source charts to W also agree, and glue on C to j. The equality j ≫ p = h holds on C and therefore globally.

The inverse image under j of a glued chart is its original source chart. To verify this, test in another source chart: membership in the glued chart is equivalent to membership in the prescribed thickened overlap, whose inverse image is the source overlap. Thus the pullback square on each chart identifies the restriction of j with the supplied local first order immersion. Closed immersion is local on the target, so j is a closed immersion. The global kernel ideal restricts to the local kernels; their squares vanish, so its square vanishes on the open cover and hence globally.

Take D to be the canonical glued open cover of W. The pullback identifications from the preceding step transport the local universal properties to precisely IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening ((D.pullback₁ j).f k ≫ h) (D.pullbackHom j k) (D.f k ≫ p), as claimed.

lean.statement:
theorem universalFirstOrderThickening_gluedAtlas
    {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ X) (C : Z.OpenCover.{u})
    (Z' : C.I₀ → Scheme.{u}) (i : ∀ k, C.X k ⟶ Z' k)
    (h' : ∀ k, Z' k ⟶ X)
    (H : ∀ k, IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening (C.f k ≫ h) (i k) (h' k)) :
    ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (j : Z ⟶ W) (p : W ⟶ X) (D : W.OpenCover.{u}),
      IsFirstOrderThickening j ∧ j ≫ p = h ∧
        ∀ k, IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening ((D.pullback₁ j).f k ≫ h)
          (D.pullbackHom j k) (D.f k ≫ p)
